title: Creator of Anthropic's Claude Code wants you to stop micromanaging your AI
excerpt: Boris Cherny, creator of Anthropic's Claude Code, said users don't need to get too specific with their instructions for modern models.
content_html:
By Lloyd Lee

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

If AI users are the new bosses and agents are the new employees, then the creator of Anthropic's popular coding agent has a piece of evergreen management advice: Stop micromanaging your AI.

Boris Cherny, the creator of Anthropic's Claude Code, said at a Y Combinator event on Saturday that one common mistake he sees from Claude users is giving overly detailed, step-by-step instructions because they underestimate the tasks a model can handle.

"They're like, 'I want you to do this, but I want you to do it in this way, this way, this way. You must do one, then two, then three, then four,'" Cherny said. "For modern models, that's actually really not the way to do it."

Instead, Cherny said users should be specific about the outcome while giving the model more freedom to decide how to get there. He recommended describing the task, setting the guardrails, and defining what a successful completion looks like.

"Then just go let the model cook and come back in a little bit," he said. "I think it'll surprise you."

Cherny's advice reflects how quickly AI models can improve, potentially rendering older prompting habits obsolete. Cherny said his approach may not have worked six months ago, but it does with today's more capable models.

Google Brain cofounder Andrew Ng shared a similar idea last year, calling it "lazy prompting" — when users provide minimal instructions as models get smarter.

"We add details to the prompt only when they are needed," Ng said.

Cherny said Anthropic employees are also finding new capabilities as they experiment with the company's models. He estimated that there are probably dozens, if not hundreds, of useful abilities that have yet to be discovered.

So, AI power users: Don't repeat the same mistakes bad managers make. You could be getting in your AI's way.

作者：Lloyd Lee 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

如果人工智能用户是新老板，代理是新员工，那么 Anthropic 流行编码代理的创建者有一条常青的管理建议：停止对人工智能进行微观管理。

Anthropic 的 Claude Code 的创建者 Boris Cherny 在周六的 Y Combinator 活动上表示，他从 Claude 用户那里看到的一个常见错误是给出过于详细的分步说明，因为他们低估了模型可以处理的任务。

“他们会说，‘我希望你这样做，但我希望你以这种方式、这样、这样的方式来做。 你必须做一件事，然后做两件事，然后做三件事，然后做四件事，’”切尔尼说。 “对于现代模型来说，这实际上并不是正确的做法。”

相反，切尔尼表示，用户应该具体说明结果，同时给予模型更多自由来决定如何达到目标。 他建议描述任务，设置护栏，并定义成功完成的样子。

“然后让模型做饭，一会儿再回来，”他说。 “我想这会让你感到惊讶。”

切尔尼的建议反映了人工智能模型改进的速度有多快，有可能使旧的提示习惯变得过时。 切尔尼表示，他的方法在六个月前可能行不通，但对于当今功能更强大的模型来说却行之有效。

Google Brain 联合创始人 Andrew Ng 去年也分享了类似的想法，称其为“惰性提示”——随着模型变得更加智能，用户提供最少的指令。

“我们仅在需要时才在提示中添加详细信息，”吴说。

Cherny 表示，Anthropic 员工在尝试公司模型时也发现了新的功能。 他估计，可能有数十种（甚至数百种）有用的能力尚未被发现。

所以，人工智能的高级用户：不要重复糟糕的管理者所犯的同样的错误。 你可能会妨碍你的人工智能。
